clusters.lens: Management/control planes of the security and infrastructure estate were the exploited surface, and in each case remediation is not the patch
clusters.why_on_fire: All five are confirmed exploited or confirmed abused in the wild; four are KEV-listed; every one requires credential/key rotation or a compromise assessment beyond the upgrade, and the FortiOS and BMC cases explicitly defeat a remediation the operator already believes they performed.

clusters.lens: Water/wastewater OT PLC attacks went from one state to seven inside the week, with a European exposure count published in the same window
clusters.why_on_fire: Cross-day escalation; no CVE required, only an internet-reachable controller; a Censys scan in-window puts 86% of exposed Siemens S7-1200 units in four European countries.

clusters.lens: Russian state-nexus targeting of travelling government and diplomatic staff through hospitality captive portals
clusters.why_on_fire: Active since early May 2026 worldwide; named target population is travelling government and diplomatic staff; device-code phishing added to landing pages from 16 July. A federal SOC whose staff travelled since May and took no action has an unexamined exposure.

candidate_patterns.lens: Every authentication bypass disclosed this week came from code treating an attacker-supplied value as proof of identity — the check ran, it just validated the wrong thing
candidate_patterns.distinct_from_prior_weekly: W29's weekly-multi-day (identity-trust-relationship-abuse) was about abusing legitimately-granted OAuth consent, tokens and helpdesk process. This is a code-level defect class: the identity input itself is attacker-controlled and the validating code accepts it.

candidate_patterns.lens: Neither KEV nor a patch was available for several of the week's exploited or exploitation-imminent flaws — both of the standard prioritisation feeds failed in the same window
candidate_patterns.distinct_from_prior_weekly: No prior weekly consolidated the 'no KEV entry and/or no fix exists' failure mode as a pattern in its own right.

list_4_sector_victim_patterns.lens: In nearly every confirmed European public-sector and CI incident this week the entry point was an already-legitimate account or credential, not an exploit
list_4_sector_victim_patterns.distinct_from_prior_weekly: W30's sector entry was third-party/shared-platform/fiduciary access plus victims walking back 'not affected' claims. This week's thread is narrower and different: the credential itself was valid, and the attacker used the platform's own legitimate export/admin function.

list_5_incidents_recap.lens: Criminal claims outran confirmation in every direction this week — a fabricated victim list containing one real government breach, a blast-radius claim on a single outlet, an attribution the victim will not confirm
list_5_incidents_recap.distinct_from_prior_weekly: W30's disclosure-pattern limb was victims under-claiming and being contradicted by the leak. This is the inverse polarity — operators over-claiming — and it is directly actionable for anyone triaging leak-site feeds.

candidate_patterns.lens: This week's tradecraft was engineered against the analyst's environment rather than the endpoint agent — samples that will not detonate in a sandbox, will not decrypt away from the host they infected, and produce telemetry indistinguishable from the victim's own activity
candidate_patterns.distinct_from_prior_weekly: W29's research entry was EDR blinding (hooking AFD IOCTLs, patient collection). W30's was C2 through trusted infrastructure. This is host-binding and environment-keying: the anti-analysis control is the sample refusing to run or decrypt outside its intended victim.

candidate_patterns.lens: AI: the autonomous-operator claim got measured this week and under-performed manual work, while the AI toolchain itself became the vulnerable surface and AI-assisted review failed as an assurance control
candidate_patterns.disposition: update_of the W30 strategic entry — delta only, because the theme is already consolidated
